analysis: The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md (a v0.10.13 candidate header and highlights added at head lines 11-45). The two supplied units are unchanged historical changelog text (head lines 2219-2651), so the changed lines themselves are not in the supplied numbered text. I examined the surrounding entries against the threat model. They describe behavior already shipped, not new code. These entries touch: the enabled_models filter refusing coordinator load_model/prefetch_model (TB-002, T-027); the sandbox installer download and --plan run as the Mac owner (TB-013, T-061); update --rollback with quarantine and the watchdog swap (T-043, T-013); the encrypted SSD prefix cache for Gemma/Qwen/GLM tensor-parallel (T-041, SEC-035, with record scoping and AES-GCM unchanged); and the cluster approvals and registration flow (TB-002, TB-011). The text is documentation only and carries no executable change. I found no security control weakened, and no claim that contradicts the threat model such as raising the 30-minute TTL, enabling plaintext, or dropping authentication. One item worth noting: the changelog says 'Setup's output is line-buffered' and describes the sandbox flow never passing --force. Neither affects any control. I could not see the patch for lines 11-45 beyond the excerpt, which is truncated. The highlights describe a Gemma loop-exit-thinking feature (#2040) and a stop fix (#2042), but those code changes are not in the supplied evidence. If the code PR is reviewed elsewhere, the next pass should check whether the loop-exit injection (closing the thought, an 8,192-token cap) interacts with prefix-cache keys or logprobs. The changelog says it is disabled with logprobs and on pairs.
